title: Coronary calcium score
what: A short CT scan of the heart without contrast dye. It measures how much calcium is in the heart's arteries. Calcium is a sign of hardened arteries.
why: To estimate the risk of heart disease in people with no symptoms, when the doctor is deciding on prevention.
duration: usually 10 to 15 minutes in the room; the scan itself takes a few seconds; results the same or the next day
tell_doctor: If you are or might be pregnant
If you have stents or had bypass surgery. This test may not suit you
If your pulse is fast or irregular

prepare.title: Prep
prepare.text: No injection is needed. You can eat and drink.

prepare.title: Coffee
prepare.text: You are usually asked to skip coffee and energy drinks that day. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: No metal on the chest. Better to take off an underwire bra and necklaces.

bring: Cholesterol test results, if you have them
steps: ECG stickers are put on your chest
You lie on your back with your arms behind your head
The table moves into the ring of the scanner
Hold your breath for a few seconds while the image is taken
feel: It does not hurt. There are no injections
after: You can go about your day right away
The result is a number, the calcium score. Take it to a cardiologist or your doctor

faq.q: What does a score of zero mean?
faq.a: No calcium was found in the heart's arteries. This usually means a low risk in the next few years.

faq.q: If calcium is found, does that mean a heart attack?
faq.a: No. It is a sign of deposits in the arteries. Your doctor will decide if you need prevention or more tests.

reminders.text: Calcium score scan tomorrow. No coffee in the morning. Wear clothes with no metal.
